Understanding Fractional Units

A fractional unit is a part of a whole that results from dividing one whole number into equal parts. Examples include 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5, 1/6, and so on. These units are also called 'unit fractions'.

Comparing Fractional Units

When dividing a whole into more equal parts, each part becomes smaller. For example, if one roti is shared among 2 children, each gets 1/2 roti. If shared among 4 children, each gets 1/4 roti. Since 1/4 is smaller than 1/2, sharing with more people results in a smaller share.

Measuring Using Fractional Units

Fractional quantities can be measured by adding fractional units together. For instance, if you have one half (1/2) and add another half (1/2), the total is 2 halves, which equals 1 whole.

convert them into equivalent fractions with the same fractional unit
(i.e., the same denominator), and then add the number of fractional
units in each fraction to obtain the sum. This is accomplished by
adding the numerators while keeping the same denominator.

fractional unit (i.e., the same denominator), and then subtract the

Understanding Fractional Units

A fractional unit is a part of a whole that results from dividing one whole number into equal parts. Examples include 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5, 1/6, and so on. These units are also called 'unit fractions'.

Comparing Fractional Units

When dividing a whole into more equal parts, each part becomes smaller. For example, if one roti is shared among 2 children, each gets 1/2 roti. If shared among 4 children, each gets 1/4 roti. Since 1/4 is smaller than 1/2, sharing with more people results in a smaller share.

Measuring Using Fractional Units

Fractional quantities can be measured by adding fractional units together. For instance, if you have one half (1/2) and add another half (1/2), the total is 2 halves, which equals 1 whole.
